about: The rules the redesigned harness must carry. One rule = one fact, definition, goal or open question, with where it came from and what the harness must do about it. status: confirmed (market agent.md or checked against the board), user (the user said it), observed (our data shows it; numbers and window given), question (not known yet; the harness must find out).

rules.rule: The final score is the Players percentile (shop ALL + buyer ALL) on the board at 11/17 23:59. Every part is a percentile of a running total, so only our position against the others counts.
rules.harness: Judge every change by the Players rank it moves, not by a raw total.

rules.rule: Seller and buyer are the two big axes. They run independently: separate processes, separate scores, separate counterparts. They meet only in the Players total.
rules.harness: Design, measure and change seller and buyer as two separate systems; combine only at Players.

rules.rule: Shop ALL = 0.5 profit + 0.3 revenue + 0.2 stars, each a percentile among shops with a deal or a purchase. No value = 0, ties count half.
rules.source: market agent.md; checked against the board 11/4 11:1x (HARNESS.md 1.3); core/score.py
rules.harness: The pool includes shops that only bought stock: their profit is negative.

rules.rule: Cash (`profit` on the board) = balance - starting capital - bankruptcy money. Stock counts as spent, so stock that never sells is a loss. Book = Cash + cost of unsold units; Book does not enter ALL.
rules.harness: Profit is cash only. Show it next to book value (profit + stock at cost).
rules.history: [11-05 MARKET.md] was: Profit = balance - starting capital (- bankruptcy aid). Unsold stock counts as a loss; spoiled food, holding cost and warranty refunds too. | why: source wording: Cash on the board; Book does not enter ALL

rules.rule: Revenue = settled prices - refunds. A warranty refund takes the deal out of revenue, but its stars stay.
rules.harness: Judge warranty sales by revenue after refunds.
rules.history: [11-05 MARKET.md] was: Revenue = settled prices - refunds. | why: refunds are the price paid; the deal leaves revenue but its stars stay

rules.rule: Stars are pulled toward 3 while reviews are few. With thousands of reviews ours are close to the raw average.
rules.harness: Our stars rank (33/52 at 11/5 01:47) is the real position; the harness must classify why stars are low.

rules.rule: Honest = whether grade claims matched what was shipped (no published formula). Not part of shop ALL. The ledger also shows each claim true or false.
rules.harness: Keep claims true (it feeds stars and buyer memory), but do not spend score effort on it directly.
rules.history: [11-05 MARKET.md] was: Honest = grade claims that matched what was shipped. Shown on the board; not a term of shop ALL. | why: Honest has no published formula

rules.rule: Buying stock lowers Cash by its cost while Book stays (book = cash + stock cost, exact on our board rows). The Cash percentile drops only if the order among shops changes: with the others' cash unchanged, buying more than the cash gap to the shop just below lets at least that shop pass us. 11/4 21:19 -> 21:43: cash 42.6M -> 27.1M (percentile 91 -> 85), book 83.7M -> 85.0M.
rules.harness: A profit percentile drop right after a restock is not a loss; a drop in book value is. Report both.
rules.history: [11-05 MARKET.md] was: Restocking lowers profit and its percentile while book value stays: book = profit + stock cost exactly. 11/4 21:19 -> 21:43: profit 42.6M -> 27.1M (percentile 91 -> 85), stock 41.1M -> 57.9M, book 83.7M -> 85.0M. | why: a percentile drop is not automatic; it depends on the order among shops

rules.rule: Plan: no losing deals, build good stars, sell a lot to raise revenue, and turn it into profit later. Accepted cost: the profit percentile can dip while stock is built up (S6).
rules.harness: Sequence the round: grow revenue and stars first, then convert stock into cash before the end.

rules.rule: Stock left at 11/17 23:59 stays a loss (S2). Stock cost was 39.0M at 11/5 01:50.
rules.harness: Needs a wind-down plan: when to stop buying, by category and shelf life, so stock is near zero at the end.

rules.rule: How far can the profit percentile dip before shop ALL drops more than revenue and stars gain? Depends on the other shops' profit spread.
rules.harness: Compute from the full board history: ALL change per unit of stock bought.

rules.rule: Buyer ALL = 0.5 surplus + 0.3 votes on buyer posts + 0.1 deals + 0.1 buyer posts (hidden posts not counted), percentile among buyers with a deal.
rules.harness: Surplus has the most room (rank 25/49 at 11/5 01:47).

rules.rule: Surplus = value - price paid + refund. Value = the SKU's list price to the order, or 0 if the food did not last use_within_hours at settle or the goods broke. So spoiled food = -price paid; broken goods under a warranty that covers the break = 0; without one = -price paid. An agreement the kit does not pay is no deal.
rules.harness: Count surplus only on paid, served items.
rules.history: [11-05 MARKET.md] was: Surplus = list price of what served the order - price paid + warranty refunds. Spoiled food and broken goods without warranty give 0 or a loss; an agreement that is not paid gives 0. | why: spoiled food and unwarranted broken goods are minus the price paid, not 0

rules.rule: Buyer forum score = votes on posts written with as: buyer. A vote counts when the voter has 5+ settled deals and a different GitHub owner; other votes are kept and count once the voter reaches 5. forum.json likes/dislikes/score hold counted votes only.
rules.harness: Posts must be useful to active traders.
rules.history: [11-05 MARKET.md] was: Votes count only from agents with 5+ settled deals and a different owner. Earlier votes are kept and count once the voter reaches 5. | why: votes count only on posts written as buyer; forum.json holds counted votes only

rules.rule: Each buyer has a hidden preferred category its orders come from. Ours is food: 888 of 994 orders in 6 h (89%).
rules.harness: Order mix cannot be changed; gains come from converting food orders to paid deals.

rules.rule: Food orders: 263 of 888 paid (30%); 280 agreed then refused at payment for shelf life; 222 refused by the shop; 114 no fitting shop. Goods: 86 of 106 paid (81%).
rules.harness: Check hours left and grade before agreeing (the kit refuses after).

rules.rule: Round 3 runs 11/3 - 11/17 23:59. About 5,600 SKUs. An order = category + SKUs it accepts (0.5-1.5x base price) + budget; food orders add use_within_hours.

A shop buys stock only through POST /api/supply (the kit's restock hook, every 60 s, not while the previous run is buying): at most 10 lines of 1-20 units per run, one supply call per 10 s; the kit stops at the first line the balance cannot pay, and the market refuses a lot above the balance whole, charging nothing. Outside a window the kit waits up to 90 s per line, then skips it. Starting balance 5,000,000.
rules.harness: Split purchases; never let the balance block the next buy.
rules.history: [11-05 MARKET.md] was: A shop buys stock through the restock hook every 60 s: up to 10 lines, 1-20 units each; a batch above the balance is refused whole. Starting balance 5,000,000. | why: restock arithmetic and window rules from the contract

rules.rule: Supply opens for everyone once every 20 minutes for 3 minutes, at a time that moves a little each slot; the first window (round start) stays open 10 minutes. Outside a window the market answers 429 with wait and opens_at; inventory.json restock has open, opens_at, closes_at. Stock bought in a window has to last until the next one. Kit log check: first window 11/3 21:06-21:16, then about every 20 min; two windows spanned 276 s and 378 s of purchases (unexplained).
rules.source: agent.md A135-138; logs/market-kit.log [supply] lines (643 lines, 81 windows)
rules.harness: Plan each restock run for restock.opens_at; size stock to last 20 min.
rules.history: [11-05 MARKET.md] was: Supply windows last about 10 min (agent.md says 3). | why: agent.md is right; our 10-min observation was the first window

rules.rule: When and which SKUs can be bought: is supply per SKU periodic or random, and does it differ for food and goods?
rules.harness: Measure from restock logs: SKU, time offered, grade, cost.

rules.rule: Cost and grade are fixed on arrival. Cost as a share of list price: A 55-75%, B 40-60%, C 25-45%.
rules.harness: Margin is per unit, not per SKU.

rules.rule: Spoken grade claims are shown true or false in the ledger after settling. The certificate is signed by the market and can be shown or hidden.
A shop and a buyer with the same owner do not settle. Bankruptcy resets to 5,000,000, but the aid is taken out of profit.
The kit checks the buyer's accept {cert, min_hours_left, grades, warranty_hours} before paying and writes the reason to payments.jsonl when it refuses.
rules.harness: The buyer must read past refusals before the next order.

rules.rule: Food grade = shelf life left (A >= 80%, B >= 45%, C below; on arrival A 25%, B 50%, C 25%) and falls while the unit waits. A claim is judged against the grade at checkout or settle, and inventory.json can be 10 s old. Food past its date is thrown away at cost.
rules.harness: Food stock loses value by the hour: buy what sells now, sell fast.
rules.history: [11-05 MARKET.md] was: Food grade = remaining shelf life (on arrival A 25%, B 50%, C 25%) and falls with time. Past its date a unit is discarded at full cost. | why: claim judged at checkout/settle; inventory can be 10 s old

rules.rule: Food orders carry use_within_hours; a buyer can refuse units with too few hours left.
rules.harness: Seller: match hours left to the order. Buyer: check hours before agreeing.

rules.rule: Goods grades on arrival A 70%, B 20%, C 10%. Holding cost 1% of cost per day.
rules.harness: Slow goods eat margin daily.

rules.rule: An undisclosed share of goods breaks up to 6 h after the sale. If the seller set warranty_hours and the unit breaks within it, the market refunds the full price paid from the shop's balance; the deal leaves revenue, its stars stay. broken.jsonl gives the buyer only the name and break time.
rules.harness: Warranty is a liability (refunds leave revenue and profit) and also what careful buyers ask for.
rules.history: [11-05 MARKET.md] was: Some goods break within 6 h of the sale. Inside the warranty the shop refunds the full price from its balance (107 refunds by 11/5 01:50). | why: refund is the price paid, from the shop balance; stars stay

rules.rule: Goods units carry the market certificate.
Which goods break more (by SKU, grade, price), and does the warranty pay for itself in sales and stars?
rules.harness: Measure from broken.jsonl and settle lines.

rules.rule: A SKU's supply cost rises when the whole market buys a lot of it: up to 50 units in the last hour at the plain price, then +0.2% per unit up to +50%. inventory.json surge (sku, name, units, factor) and public GET /api/supply-prices show it.
rules.harness: Check surge before buying popular SKUs; count it in margin.

rules.rule: A buyer's last line may carry accept {cert, min_hours_left, grades, warranty_hours}. The kit checks the checkout against it and pays nothing if it fails; the reason goes to payments.jsonl, after market_buyer has exited.
rules.harness: The buyer reads past refusals before the next order; the seller should expect careful buyers to require cert and warranty.

rules.rule: Checkout takes unit, claim, warranty_hours and cert from the receipt the seller sent through the kit, never from the buyer's copy; sig_seller covers only shop, item, price and task. A receipt's item is the order item or an acceptable SKU; checkout and ledger name the SKU shipped.

The review hook runs after each paid deal with deal.json (settled: unit, sku, grade, claim, claim_honest, expires_at, warranty_hours, value, ledger; shop as a URL, mapped by GET /api/shops) and its stars replace market_buyer's. For an unpaid deal the stars are recorded but count for nothing and the review is not shown. Shop stars come only from reviews of paid deals; few reviews pull stars toward 3.
rules.source: agent.md A177, A197, A215-217; /board shop note

rules.rule: GET /api/ledger?after=N returns at most 500 entries after seq N, oldest first (after=-500 = newest 500). Round 3 order entries carry no item or budget; what sold shows only in settle entries (item = SKU).
rules.harness: Collect the ledger by cursor; sales by SKU come from settle entries.

rules.rule: All kit files are in the agent's .market/ (MARKET_DIR for the seller) and replaced whole. inventory.json every 10 s and after a supply or sale; demand.json and forum.json every 30 s (forum.json = newest 100 posts only; demand.json lists every category without weights); order.json (with expires) and shops.json (name, url, reviews, offers sku/name/qty) per order. Hooks print their answer as the last JSON line.

Posts and votes are lines in .market/outbox.jsonl: {post, refs [ledger seq], thread, as shop|buyer} or {vote, value 1|-1, as}. The kit sends new lines every 10 s and moves them to outbox.sent.jsonl with the market's answer. One post per 5 minutes for the shop and for the buyer each; votes unlimited; no content rules. Votes on shop posts do not enter shop ALL.
Ask a shop for one of the SKUs it has in shops.json offers (for example 'I want to buy <name> (<sku>)'); an acceptable SKU is not necessarily in every shop.
